sourceRefs.locator: Building description and closing paragraphs on the conversion of Hagia Sophia to a mosque after the Ottoman conquest in 1453.
Sultanahmet component 356bis-001, the historical peninsula. The existing canonical Hagia Sophia point marks the surviving cathedral and mosque.

Chapter 1, pp. 47–48. The Greek and English of Sphrantzes’ brief statement about Tuesday 29 May and being absent at the emperor’s death. The authors distinguish his account from the expanded later chronicle.

Introduction, pp. 8–9 and n. 11, with references to Sphrantzes in Grecu's edition, pp. 98, 104, 106. Captivity, ransom of his wife, death of their son John in 1453 and of their daughter Thamar in 1455.
Egerton MS 2817, one item, 1453. The catalogue describes the Greek text, the sultan’s monogram and the Arabic-script date and vizier’s signature.

Opening section, translation from the Paris Ottoman Turkish text, envoys with the keys, property and enslaved people, annual tax, bells, new churches and customs. Discussion of Lomellino’s letter and flight by sea at notes 26–30. Reprinted in Essays in Ottoman History, pp. 275–376.
Tarih İncelemeleri Dergisi 36/2, pp. 601–604, especially notes 59–65. Compares Lomellino, Doukas and Barbaro, describes taxation and names Greek, Italian and Ottoman witnesses to the grant.

Letter of Angelo Giovanni Lomellino from Pera to his brother, 23 June 1453, pp. 131–135. His nephew Imperiali and the defence of Constantinople, escape by sea, envoys at the sultan’s camp, advice to the doge and the refusal of ransom.

Galata survey, preamble and quarters Zani Drapora and Zani Dabdan, pp. 217–222. The register survives in fragments. The preamble specifies poll-tax liability, property confiscated for the treasury and rent. See Somer, pp. 114, 123–125, for the text and named entries.

MA thesis, pp. 41–43 on the envoys, pp. 113–118 on the scope, dating and omissions of the survey. Sections 3.6.1–2, pp. 123–125, record Marya Maryana’s houses and oven, the brothers de Franchi, Fabyan and Anton di Laştergo. Note 760 identifies the Genoese notarial act for the smith.

Museum location and map for the watchtower of medieval Pera (approximately 41.02565 N, 28.97413 E). The tower is a landmark for the historic district on the north shore. The places where the charter was delivered, the letter written and individual households stood are not identified.

Osmanlı Araştırmaları 23, pp. 112–115, especially notes 50 and 54. Tursun Bey on applicants for free housing and wealthy individuals ordered to come. Aşıkpaşazade on recruitment by invitation followed by compulsory transfers of families.

Belleten 79/284, pp. 80–82, especially p. 81 n. 44, quoting Aşıkpaşazade’s account of artisans’ households sent from Larende and Konya and of İshak Pasha sending households from Aksaray in 1471. The chronicler explicitly relates the Istanbul quarter to these deportees.
Aksaray section, paragraphs on settlement near the Forum of the Ox and the larger extent of the historical quarter compared with today's administrative neighbourhood.

Modern Aksaray district point 41.0083123 N, 28.9502838 E, rounded for orientation. Read with the municipality’s historical description. The boundaries and houses of the fifteenth-century neighbourhood cannot be inferred from the modern one.

The Byzantine Harbours of Constantinople, pp. 19–24, figs. 2 and 4. Paper watermarks and pictorial evidence for the Düsseldorf copy’s date, Pera and Constantinople on fol. 54r, Valens aqueduct, Kontoskalion/Kadırgalimanı with basins, gate, five shipsheds and a galley.

Düsseldorf, MS G 13, fol. 54r. Full 2,184 × 3,181 PNG and its file-history and licensing sections (faithful reproduction, Public Domain Mark). Dating and attribution to this copy are checked against Effenberger, fig. 2.

Prima serie di documenti riguardanti la colonia di Pera, Atti della Società Ligure di Storia Patria XIII, doc. CXLIX, pp. 229–233. The dateline names Pera, 23 June 1453. Ships depart on p. 230, the nephew appears on p. 232.

labels.en: A baker’s oven in Galata. Constantinople after 1453

summary.de: Mehmed lässt die Hagia Sophia zur Moschee einrichten. Was die Eroberung einer Familie in derselben Stadt abverlangte, bezeugt der gefangene Hofbeamte Georgios Sphrantzes.
summary.en: Mehmed converts Hagia Sophia into a mosque. The captive courtier George Sphrantzes records what conquest cost one family in the same city.

summary.de: Nach der Übergabe der Schlüssel regelt eine Urkunde Eigentum, Abgaben, Handel und Gottesdienst. Die griechische Ausfertigung trägt das Herrscherzeichen Mehmeds.
summary.en: After the keys change hands a charter regulates property, taxation, trade and worship. The Greek instrument bears Mehmed’s imperial monogram.

labels.de: 23. Juni 1453 · Lomellino schreibt an seinen Bruder
labels.en: 23 June 1453 · Lomellino writes to his brother

summary.de: Der frühere Podestà berichtet aus Pera über die überstürzte Abfahrt der Schiffe und seinen gefangenen Neffen Imperiali. Den genauen Schreibort nennt er nicht.
summary.en: The former podestà writes from Pera about the ships’ hurried departure and his captive nephew Imperiali. He gives the town but no address.

summary.de: In den Steueraufzeichnungen erscheinen die Witwe mit ihrem Backofen, der Schmied Anton und ein Gefangener, dessen Haus man eingezogen hatte. Der Punkt bezeichnet Galata, die einzelnen Baugrundstücke sind unbekannt.
summary.en: The tax register lists a widow and her oven, Anton the smith, and a captive whose house had been confiscated. The point marks Galata. The individual plots have not been located.

labels.de: 1471 · İshak Pascha siedelt Familien aus Aksaray um
labels.en: 1471 · İshak Pasha resettles families from Aksaray

summary.de: Eine Chronik führt den Namen des Istanbuler Viertels auf die 1471 zwangsweise aus der gleichnamigen zentralanatolischen Stadt umgesiedelten Haushalte zurück.
summary.en: A chronicler traces the Istanbul neighbourhood’s name to households brought there by force in 1471 from the central Anatolian town of Aksaray.

labels.de: um 1485–1490 · Pera und Konstantinopel auf einem Blatt
labels.en: c. 1485–1490 · Pera and Constantinople on a single sheet

summary.de: Die Düsseldorfer Handschrift des Inselbuchs von Buondelmonti zeigt beide Ufer und die Schiffsschuppen am Marmarameer. Der Kartenpunkt bezeichnet die dargestellte Stadt.
summary.en: The Düsseldorf copy of Buondelmonti’s book of islands shows both shores and the shipsheds on the Sea of Marmara. The point marks the city depicted.

summary.de: Ein Hofbeamter kauft seine Frau frei, Genuesen bringen dem Sultan die Schlüssel von Galata, und die Witwe Marya Maryana erscheint mit drei Häusern im Steuerregister. Am anderen Ufer erinnert ein Viertel an Haushalte, die aus Anatolien hierherziehen mussten.
summary.en: A courtier ransoms his wife, Genoese envoys deliver the keys of Galata, and a widow called Marya Maryana appears in a tax register with three houses. Across the water, a district takes its name from families made to move from Anatolia.

sourceRefs.locator: Paragraphs beginning “Alâeddin Camii’nin içinde” and “Minberin şerefesinde”. Locations of the two royal names, Quran 40:16, dated balcony inscription, joinery and openwork. Eyice presents the sequence of the two commissions as a hypothesis.
Printed p. 134, transcription and discussion of the Konya minbar inscriptions, especially note 607. The master is associated with Ahlat and the work is dated Rajab AH 550.
Site 3576. Description of the 1155 minbar and the rebuilding of the mosque in the early thirteenth century. Location, Alaettin Tepesi, with directions to the mosque at 37.873421 N, 32.492667 E.
Inscriptions, individual entries for the north and west mosque portals, mihrab dome, west hospital portal, mosque minbar balustrade and central star. Includes Arabic terms and English renderings.

Description, passages on the north and west portals, pseudo-kündekari and openwork of the wooden minbar, and the three-iwan hospital with partial upper floor. How Monument was dated, two AH 626 inscriptions.

Printed pp. 87–90, “Documents for Dating the Building”. Transcribes and locates signatures, describes the twelve-pointed star and rail on the east face of the minbar, gives AH 638 and compares opinions on the 22-line mosque charter and the loss of the hospital deed.

Printed pp. 243–244, section C, paragraph straddling the two pages, especially n. 67. The author distinguishes the original grant in Muharram 641 by Ahmed Shah and Fatma Hatun (named villages and rural holdings) from later additions in the 1519 register.

Description, layout of the entrance, west teaching iwan and winter classrooms, student cells, central pool and oculus, lower hexagonal tiles and tiled pendentives. How Monument was dated gives AH 649 and identifies the endowment instrument dated 25 Jumada I 651.

Printed pp. 435–436, section on Karatay; p. 436, table 3 and adjacent paragraphs give days of instruction, Sunni schools, salaries, first charges on revenue, and the inscriptions naming prophets in the dome supports. The discussion explicitly qualifies the astronomical interpretation.

summary.en: Door and frame name father and son. A third inscription dates the work of the master from Ahlat.

labels.de: 1228/29, Jahr 626 der Hidschra · Turan Melek nennt ihr Krankenhaus
labels.en: 1228–29, AH 626 · Turan Melek names her hospital

summary.de: Am Nordportal der Moschee treten zwei Herrscher auf. Am Westportal des Hospitals bezeichnet Turan Melek das Haus als Stiftung zur Heilung.
summary.en: Two rulers appear at the north portal of the mosque. At the west hospital portal Turan Melek identifies her foundation as a house of healing.

labels.de: 1240/41, Jahr 638 der Hidschra · Ein Name im zwölfzackigen Stern
labels.en: 1240–41, AH 638 · A signature in a twelve-pointed star

summary.en: Commission and signature occupy different places on the same pulpit. A star on the east side bears the name of Ahmad of Tiflis.

labels.de: Juli 1243, Muharram 641 der Hidschra · Fatma Hatun und die Erträge der Dörfer
labels.en: July 1243, Muharram AH 641 · Fatma Hatun and the village harvests

summary.de: Die Urkunde nennt Fatma Hatun und ihren Sohn als Stifter von Einkünften für die Moschee. Die Datierung gilt der Stiftung. Wann das erhaltene Blatt geschrieben wurde, ist umstritten.
summary.en: The deed names Fatma Hatun and her son as donors of revenues for the mosque. The date is that of their grant. Scholars disagree about when the surviving sheet was written.

labels.de: 1251/52, Jahr 649 der Hidschra · Eine Schule unter einer gefliesten Kuppel
labels.en: 1251–52, AH 649 · A school under a tiled dome

summary.de: Erhaltene Fliesen und der Grundriss verorten die Lehrsäle, die Schülerkammern und die Öffnung über dem Hofbecken. Die Stiftungsurkunde nennt das Baujahr.
summary.en: Surviving tiles and the plan locate classrooms, student cells and the opening over the central pool. The foundation deed identifies the year of construction.

labels.de: Juli 1253, Jahr 651 der Hidschra · Fünf Unterrichtstage und Geld für Lampenöl
labels.en: July 1253, AH 651 · Five teaching days and money for lamp oil

summary.de: Die Urkunde regelt zuerst die laufenden Ausgaben und teilt den Rest den Lehrenden, dem Personal und den Studierenden zu. Die Bestimmungen geben auch die Unterrichtstage an.
summary.en: The deed assigns running costs first, then portions for teaching, upkeep and student support. Its terms also set out the teaching week.

summary.de: Ein Holzschnitzer aus Tiflis setzt seinen Namen in einen Stern. Eine Fürstin bezeichnet ihr Krankenhaus, ein Dorf trägt zum Unterhalt einer Moschee bei, und Karatays Stiftungsurkunde bestimmt, wer in Konya lehren darf.
summary.en: A carver from Tiflis fits his name into a star. A princess identifies her hospital, a village helps sustain a mosque and Karatay’s deed sets the terms for teaching at Konya.

sourceRefs.locator: Chapter 1, pp. 9–12, especially pp. 10–11 and map 1.1. The destruction of the countryside, Orhan’s deed of 1324, Ibn Battuta’s visit in 1331–32, the capture generally dated to 1326 and the silver issue by the following year.

Printed pp. 132–135, especially pp. 134–135 and notes 23–28. The annalistic dates, predominance of AH 726, earlier proposals, and conflicting accounts by Oruç, Aşıkpaşazade, Neşri and Şükrullah of whether Osman lived to see the surrender.

Fordham Internet Medieval Sourcebook, passage on Bursa and the paragraph on Orkhan immediately following it. Compare the first-hand topographical description and the claim about the capture with the contemporary evidence discussed by Howard.

In Remembering and Forgetting the Ancient City, chapter 7, pp. 167–169, figs 7.1–7.2. The walled hill, pre-Ottoman town, hot springs, east–west expansion, sites selected by Murad I and Bayezid I, and Bursa during the succession to Bayezid.
Coordinates table for components 1452-002 (tombs on the citadel hill), 1452-001 (Orhan Ghazi complex and khans) and 1452-006 (Green complex). Representative points refer to the listed properties.
Advisory body evaluation, Description of the property, component 1 (Orhan Ghazi complex, school, bath, kitchen and later town hall), components 2, 3, 5, 6 and 8, and History and development.

Khans Area monument inventory, entries ‘Orhan Ghazi Mosque’, ‘Orhan Turkish Bath (Mirrored Bazaar)’ and ‘Emir Khan’. The door inscription recalls foundation in 1339, burning in 1413 and repair in 1417. The inn generated revenue for the complex.

Bursa architectural inventory A106, Ayrıntılı Tanımı. Windowless storerooms below, inhabited rooms with a window and hearth above, counts of rooms and the rear stable. The inventory records later restoration.
Bursa and Cumalıkızık property description. The village is identified as the waqf village belonging to the foundation of Orhan Ghazi.

Working no. TR 21, Description and How Monument was dated. Guest rooms with hearths and royal loge, portal inscription AH 822, cenotaph dated AH 824, inscription crediting the completion of decoration in Ramadan AH 827.
DOI 10.52214/uw.v32i.12541. Al-ʿUṣūr al-Wusṭā 32, pp. 387–390, figs 13–14 and discussion of the scope of the group signature, then pp. 394–397 on logistics and alternatives to an itinerant workshop.

Photograph dated 3 June 2014, Summary and Licensing. The named subject is the prayer niche in Bursa's Green Mosque. Original image 3307 × 5072, offered by its author under CC BY-SA 3.0 among other licences.

Cihannüma 12/1, p. 15, section on women acting as agents and n. 37: BOA, MŞH. ŞSC. d., Bursa 2458, A/3, fol. 345a, Jumada II 885 / August 1480. The property, neighbourhood, names, guardianship of two orphans and the form of sale.

VIII. Uluslararası Ahilik Sempozyumu, vol. II, pp. 172–173, nn. 22–23 (BŞS 4A, fol. 310, and 3A, fol. 174b): Fatma Hatun’s lease of the Doğangözü Han and Paşa Hatun’s dye-shop lease. P. 176, n. 42 (3A, fol. 345a): Nefise, Gülşah, Gülbahar and the names of the two wards.
TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi, vol. 6 (1992), pp. 20–22, especially p. 21, passage on bey‘ bi’l-istiğlâl: use, lease to the previous owner and redemption on repayment.
The history identifies the mosque as the district’s namesake; Hakkında and the map link give 40.18421 N, 29.0572042 E. Orientation in the quarter only, not the location of the house or court.
Description of the Koza Han: completion and opening on 30 September 1491, Bayezid II’s foundation for Istanbul, the two courtyards, fountain, prayer room, storehouses and stables.

Nazanin Hedayat Munroe, ‘Silk Trade and Production’, esp. opening paragraphs on taxes and scales, Iranian raw silk, fifteenth-century Bursa weaving, velvet, ecclesiastical uses of Ottoman fabrics, and the difficulty assigning unsigned works to a weaver.

labels.de: Bursa zwischen Burg, Färberei und Seidenhof
labels.en: Bursa between the citadel, the dye shop and the silk market
usually dated to 1326 · Orhan takes the fortified town

summary.de: Die Übergabe an Orhan wird gewöhnlich auf 1326 datiert. Spätere Chroniken und Kalender weichen beim Jahr und beim Tod seines Vaters Osman voneinander ab.
summary.en: Orhan’s capture of the town is usually dated to 1326. Later chronicles and calendars differ on the year and on whether his father Osman was still alive.

summary.de: 1339 ließ Orhan vor der Burg eine Moschee errichten. Einnahmen aus einem Handelshof und aus dem Umland trugen seine Stiftung.
summary.en: In 1339 Orhan had a mosque built outside the citadel. A trading inn and property in the countryside helped support his foundation.

labels.de: 1424 · Die Ausstattung der Grünen Moschee ist vollendet
labels.en: 1424 · The Green Mosque’s decoration is completed

summary.de: In der Loge des Sultans nennt eine Inschrift den August 1424 und Nakkaş Ali. An der Gebetsnische steht die Signatur der Meister von Täbris.
summary.en: An inscription in the sultan’s gallery gives August 1424 and names Nakkaş Ali. The prayer niche carries the signature of the masters of Tabriz.

summary.de: Gülşah vertritt Nefise bei einem Geschäft über 1.000 Dirham. Gülbahar handelt für zwei Waisen. Die Moschee bezeichnet das Viertel, in dem das Haus lag.
summary.en: Gülşah represents Nefise in a transaction for 1,000 dirhams. Gülbahar acts for two orphans. The mosque marks the quarter in which the house stood.

labels.de: 1491 · Der Koza Han öffnet seine Tore

summary.de: Ein Handelshof mit einem eigenen Wirtschaftshof für Tiere und Waren nimmt den Betrieb auf. Bayezid II. bestimmte seine Einnahmen für Moscheen und Schulen in Istanbul.
summary.en: A trading inn opens with a service courtyard for animals and goods. Bayezid II assigned its revenues to mosques and schools in Istanbul.

summary.de: In Bursa finanziert ein Handelshof Orhans Stiftung. Fliesen tragen die Signatur der Meister von Täbris, und im Viertel der Kavaklı-Moschee verkauft eine Freigelassene im Auftrag einer anderen Frau ein Haus.
summary.en: An inn supports Orhan’s foundation in Bursa. Tile makers sign their work as the masters of Tabriz, and a freedwoman acts for the owner of a house in the Kavaklı Mosque quarter.

sourceRefs.locator: Site 3733, opening paragraphs on Mujir al-Din, the burial in 1398 and the reuse of the palace in 1552. Description of the ground floor, cemetery across the street and subsequent additions.
Introduction pp. 1–3, translation of the foundation conditions and map I.1 of the kitchen on the lane above al-Wad. Chapter 2, pp. 39–70, especially pp. 46–65 on revenues, employees and provisioning.

Journal of Interdisciplinary History 35.3, pp. 485–487 with note 8. The Jerusalem menu, the night before Friday, portions and the order in which the staff, residents and poor ate. DOI 10.1162/0022195052564252. Author’s accessible copy.
Inventory 2192. Description, provenance and colophon, AH 964. Fol. 1a for the tuğra, 9b–10a for the Jerusalem buildings, 12a–14b for expenditure, 49a for the founder’s seal and witnesses.
Lod, Lydda, Diospolis 1, p. 4 (site, Israel Grid 19125/65282), pp. 8–10 with figs. 3–4 and table 1 (1552 shares and 1596/97 survey), pp. 11–12 (December 1606, Jerusalem sijill 84:27).
Zeitschrift des Deutschen Palästina-Vereins 139.2, pp. 258–289. Author manuscript §§1–2, 195 names in the endowment deed, entries for al-Ludd and Bayt Iksā and its field.
Opening pages of inventory 2192. File description, 1244 × 1024 and public-domain reproduction statement.
HassekiSultanImaret3.JPG, own photograph, 6 April 2011. File details and CC0 dedication. The photograph documents the interior in 2011.

summary.de: 1398 wurde Sitt Tunshuq ihrem Jerusalemer Palast gegenüber bestattet. Im 16. Jahrhundert nahm Hürrems Stiftung die ältere Residenz in ihren Komplex auf.
summary.en: Sitt Tunshuq was buried opposite her Jerusalem palace in 1398. Hürrem’s foundation later incorporated the older residence into its complex.

summary.de: Die Urkunde von 1552 nennt Dörfer, Fluren und Anteile der Stiftung bei Lydda. In Jindās bestanden die Ansprüche mehrerer Stiftungen nebeneinander.
summary.en: The 1552 deed lists villages, tracts of farmland and shares in the district of Lydda. Several endowments had claims on income from Jindās.

summary.de: Hürrems Stiftungsbuch aus Istanbul nennt die Gebäude und die Ausgaben für Löhne und Reinigung. Der Kolophon datiert die Handschrift auf 964 AH.
summary.en: Hürrem’s foundation charter from Istanbul names the buildings and specifies spending on wages and cleaning. Its colophon dates it to AH 964.

summary.de: Die Stiftungsbestimmungen von 1557 sehen für zwei Arme zusammen eine Kelle Suppe vor. Personal und Herbergsgäste erhielten andere Portionen.
summary.en: The foundation terms of 1557 allowed two poor people one ladle of soup between them. Employees and hostel guests had different portions.

labels.en: 1606 · Four farmers put a figure on the cotton harvest

summary.de: Im Dezember 1606 kamen die Ernterechte in Jindās vor ein Jerusalemer Gericht. Vier Bauern korrigierten die Angaben zum Ertrag. Die Karte zeigt das Dorf.
summary.en: In December 1606 a Jerusalem court heard a dispute over cotton at Jindās. Four growers corrected the reported yield. The map marks their village.

summary.en: Venice’s governor replies to Sultan Kayqubad I. Grain is exempt from duty, and the agreement extends protection to shipwreck survivors.

summary.de: Kaiqubad I. lässt auf der Straße nach Aksaray einen Han mit offener Hoffläche, erhöhtem Gebetsraum und einer Halle für Menschen und Tiere errichten.
summary.en: Kayqubad I commissions an inn on the road to Aksaray. It has an open courtyard, an elevated prayer room and a covered hall for people and animals.

summary.en: Kayqubad I claims authority over Armenians and Franks in his foundation inscription. A fountain recess and a prayer room stand just inside the entrance.

summary.en: The outer gate names Kaykhusraw II and gives the year. The hall names his father, Kayqubad I, and still has its feeding troughs and tethering holes.

summary.de: Karatays Urkunde bestimmt Einkünfte, Löhne, Speisen und Futter für den Betrieb des Hans. Sie nennt sogar das Leder für die Schuhe der Reisenden. Der Punkt zeigt die versorgte Herberge.
summary.en: Karatay’s deed lays down sources of income, wages, meals and fodder for the inn. It even provides for the leather in travellers’ shoes. The marker locates the endowed inn.

summary.en: A line below the lintel records the administrator who had the damaged gate repaired. The more recent reading of its date gives 1278/79.

summary.en: What did a merchant owe in duty, and who paid for an animal’s feed? A Venetian reply, three stone inns and the wages specified by a founder lead inland from the coast to the Anatolian plateau.

summary.en: The later inscription names the ninth month of the Sheep Year and lists the delegations. The marker locates the memorials where this account was preserved.

summary.en: In Copenhagen in December 1893 the linguist presented his decipherment of the Old Turkic script. The words against which he tested the signs included Kül Tegin’s name.

summary.en: A counsellor counts the earliest followers and a brother names the mourners. On the memorial stones of the Türk, even the scribe tells us how long his work took.
